annotations.title: Find how similar cases were decided

description: Given the facts of an employment situation — claim types, protected class, employer, state — analyze how similar real cases in the corpus were decided. Returns the aggregate plaintiff (employee) win rate, settlement rate, typical damages range, the topics courts discussed most in opinions employees won vs. lost, and a few representative example cases. Counts are returned at three levels (nationwide, the federal courts of the state's region, and the state) with a detailed breakdown for one level: who won, award amounts, what happened at each stage, and topics. Every figure is labeled with the level it describes. A level with few opinions returns counts without a win rate. Each example says what happened and why it matched. Topic rows record what opinions discussed, not what courts found. These are educational statistics from published opinions: a historical percentage is not any one person’s probability of winning, and the results are not a prediction or legal advice. In structured stages: won and wonPct count opinions the worker won in whole or in part (wonPct leaves rulings sent back out of its base), and sentBack counts rulings sent back to a lower court. wentForward and wentForwardPct include rulings sent back to a lower court and are kept for compatibility.

claim_types.description: Claim types alleged, snake_case, e.g. ["retaliation","wrongful_termination","discrimination","harassment"]. The single highest-value signal.

employer_name.description: Employer / defendant name, e.g. "Union Pacific Railroad". Used for a fuzzy match.

law_ids.description: Related law ids, federal or state, e.g. ["title-vii","adea","ada","fmla","flsa","fl-fcra","ca-feha"].

level.description: Which level the detailed breakdown and examples describe: "national" (default), "circuit" (federal courts of the state's region), or "state". All three levels' counts are returned either way.

narrow_to_laws.description: Only count opinions that mention one of law_ids (a federal law or its state analogue). Default false: every opinion sharing the claim type, under any law.

state.description: Two-letter US state code the situation arose in, e.g. "FL", "CA".

name: find_similar_cases

_attribution.description: Source and disclaimer for this result: Workers' Rights, its URL, the attribution line, and that the result is educational information, not legal advice.

awards.description: Recorded award amounts for the detailed level.

cohort.description: The comparison group and its size.

criteria.description: The situation facts used for matching.

damages_range.description: Typical recorded damages range, when available.

evidence_note.description: What these statistics do and do not establish.

examples.description: Representative cases and why each matched.

level.description: The level (nationwide, regional or state) given in detail.

levels.description: Counts at the nationwide, regional and state levels.

losing_factors.description: Topics most discussed in opinions the worker lost.

outcome_stats.description: Win, settlement and other outcome counts and rates.

topics_level.description: The level the topic rows describe.

winning_factors.description: Topics most discussed in opinions the worker won.
